paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. Due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates, we use the logarithmic results for comparison.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: This grouped bar chart compares perplexity values for two pruning strategies — Per-Output and Per-Layer — across different sparsity rates in the context of large language model pruning. The horizontal axis is labeled "Sparsity Rate" and displays eight categories ordered from left to right: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis is labeled "Perplexity" and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from approximately 1 to 10³ (1000), with dashed gridlines at 10¹, 10², and 10³. At each sparsity rate, two bars appear side by side: a blue bar representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar representing "Per-Layer." At lower sparsity rates (10% through 30%), both bars are very short and close in height, with perplexity values near approximately 5. At 40% and 50%, the bars remain relatively low but begin to show a slight increase. At 60%, perplexity rises noticeably to roughly 10 for both methods. At 70%, the blue Per-Output bar reaches approximately 20 and the orange Per-Layer bar reaches approximately 35. At 80%, the values increase dramatically, with the blue bar reaching approximately 500 and the orange bar approaching approximately 900. A legend is positioned in the upper-left area of the chart, identifying the blue bars as "Per-Output" and the orange bars as "Per-Layer." The logarithmic scale is used to accommodate the large range of perplexity values across sparsity rates.
model_annotations.Chinese: This figure compares the perplexity of two pruning strategies—Per-Output and Per-Layer—across different sparsity rates for large language models. The horizontal axis represents the Sparsity Rate, with categories labeled at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis represents Perplexity, displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 5 to 10³ (1000). Dashed horizontal gridlines appear at powers of ten (10¹, 10², 10³). At each sparsity rate, two bars are grouped side by side: a blue bar on the left representing Per-Output and an orange bar on the right representing Per-Layer. At 10% sparsity, both bars are very short and nearly equal, with values around 5. At 20% and 30%, the bars remain similarly low, still approximately 5 to 6. At 40%, both bars begin to increase slightly, reaching roughly 6. At 50%, the values rise to approximately 7 for Per-Output and slightly higher for Per-Layer. At 60%, the bars show a more noticeable increase, with Per-Output at roughly 10 and Per-Layer at roughly 12. At 70%, Per-Output reaches approximately 20 and Per-Layer approximately 35. At 80%, the bars grow dramatically, with Per-Output reaching approximately 500 and Per-Layer approaching approximately 900. Across all sparsity rates, the blue Per-Output bar is slightly shorter than or equal to the orange Per-Layer bar, with the difference becoming more pronounced at higher sparsity rates. The bars appear to follow an increasing trend from left to right, ordered by ascending sparsity rate. A legend is positioned in the upper-left area of the plot, showing a blue square for Per-Output and an orange square for Per-Layer. No bars appear to be visually emphasized with special shading, bolding, or annotations beyond the standard coloring.

A legend is positioned in the upper left area of the chart, showing a blue square for Per-Output and an orange square for Per-Layer. No bars appear visually emphasized beyond their color distinction.
